minutes.headline: Finance Committee set up an informal debt working group and discussed whether to pay school bus vendors; minutes approved.
minutes.summary: The committee met remotely. It agreed the debt-protocol work will run as an informal working group of no more than three members to stay within the open meeting law. The town manager reported on property closings, health insurance premium relief, Chapter 90, the interim state budget and free cash timing. Members and a caller discussed the proposed bus payment for services not delivered. Two sets of minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked why the town would pay for busing not provided if the budget is short and layoffs may follow.
Urged residents to press legislators to move the town charter bill out of the House steering committee.

votes.motion: Approve the April 9 and April 16 minutes.

budget_items.what_was_said: The health trust released reserves to members, giving a discount on the July premium to the town and school; the town manager is reserving the savings for fall town meeting.
Credits will reduce the fiscal 21 insurance payment.
The fiscal 21 Chapter 90 amount is about the same as last year's base, which was higher with a supplemental bill.
The governor signed an interim budget funding local aid at fiscal 20 cherry sheet amounts for July.

budget_items.topic: Bus payment for services not delivered
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed whether to pay bus vendors for last year's unneeded services, given vendor finances and lack of assurances.
Sale of the 17 and 23 West Street property closed June 24 and will add to certified free cash in the fall.

decisions.decision: The debt group will be run informally as a working group led by a member, not as a subcommittee, with no more than three members at a time.
The debt working group becomes a standing agenda item for the next couple of months.
Committee reorganization moved to the July 23 meeting.
The chair will re-invite legislators to update the committee on local aid.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to run the debt-protocol work as an informal working group of no more than three members, not a subcommittee, to stay within the open meeting law.
The debt working group will be a standing agenda item for the next couple of months.
Members and a caller discussed whether to pay bus vendors for services not delivered last year; no resolution was reached.
The town manager reported a health insurance premium discount, Chapter 90 and interim state budget details, and a property sale that will add to certified free cash in the fall.
Committee reorganization was moved to the July 23 meeting, and the chair will re-invite legislators to update the committee on local aid.

why_it_matters: Whether the town pays bus vendors for services not delivered is still open, and it sets a precedent for how a tight budget treats contracts when services are not provided.

The insurance savings and added free cash are being held for fall town meeting, where residents may be asked to vote on how they are used, and the interim state budget leaves local aid uncertain beyond July.
